children: Palm oil inches lower in Asian trading. Declines in soybean oil prices, weakness in competing vegetable oils, elevated Malaysian inventories and softer export demand are expected to weigh on prices, AmInvestment Bank says in a note. While a recovery in crude oil prices could offer temporary support, the overall market outlook remains volatile, it adds. AmInvestment Bank expects CPO futures to find support at 4,158 ringgit a ton and face resistance at 4,293 ringgit a ton. The Bursa Malaysia Derivatives contract for February delivery is 1 ringgit lower at 4,216 ringgit a ton. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
